vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: nanophoto-nano-banana-pro
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle provides a legitimate interface for the NanoPhoto.AI image generation service. The included Python script (scripts/nano_banana_generate.py) uses standard libraries to submit generation tasks and poll for results, with no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement the stated NanoPhoto image-generation functionality, but its registry metadata omits the required NANOPHOTO_API_KEY declaration and a few minor inconsistencies reduce confidence.

dimensions.detail: The name, description, SKILL.md, reference doc, and included Python script all consistently implement text-to-image and image-editing calls to https://nanophoto.ai. The functionality requested by the user matches what the code does. However, the registry metadata claims no required environment variables or primary credential while the instructions and script clearly require a NANOPHOTO_API_KEY — this metadata mismatch is unexpected.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md gives explicit, narrow runtime instructions: collect prompt, choose mode, provide up to 8 public image URLs for edits, submit to nanophoto.ai, and poll until completion. The script only posts JSON to the documented NanoPhoto endpoints and prints responses. It does not attempt to read arbitrary local files, other config paths, or exfiltrate unrelated data. It does, however, require that input images be public URLs (so users should not supply private/sensitive images as public links).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only skill + a bundled Python script). No external downloads, package installs, or archived extracts are present. The bundled script uses only Python standard library modules (urllib, json, argparse), so installation risk is low.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime clearly requires a single service credential (NANOPHOTO_API_KEY) to authenticate to nanophoto.ai, which is proportional to the skill's purpose. The problem is that the skill's registry metadata does not declare this required env var or a primary credential — that omission is an incoherence that could hide expected capability/permission requests from users. No other unrelated credentials or secrets are requested by the code or docs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not force-included (always: false) and does not request system-wide persistence or modify other skills' configurations. It will only act when invoked and the script does not attempt to write agent configs or escalate privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill's code and docs implement the NanoPhoto image-generation API and are consistent with each other, but the registry metadata fails to declare the required NANOPHOTO_API_KEY. Before installing: (1) Treat the API key like any other service secret — only provide a key scoped to your NanoPhoto account and store it securely in the skill's env settings or as a throwaway/test key first. (2) Inspect the bundled script (it is included) and confirm you are comfortable with it sending prompt text and any provided public image URLs to https://nanophoto.ai. Do not provide private or sensitive images as public URLs. (3) Ask the publisher to correct the registry metadata to list NANOPHOTO_API_KEY (and mark it as the primary credential) so the skill's declared permissions match its actual behavior. If you cannot verify the source or prefer caution, use a separate/test account or decline installation.
